hint.aiRootCauseAnalysis: AI Root Cause Analysis performs the following tasks:
hint.extractTopology: 1. Extracts the topology from the faulty business and sends it to the AI model for memorization.
hint.sendAlertInfo: 2. Sends all related alert information of the faulty business to the AI model to remember all alerts.
hint.applyRules: 3. Provides the AI model with a set of rules to imitate troubleshooting experts and gradually narrow down the suspected root cause nodes.
hint.provideMetrics: 4. Provides the AI model with Polaris metrics for the confirmed suspected root cause nodes to assist users in choosing the root cause direction.
hint.generateReport: 5. Generates a failure report based on the root cause direction to validate the accuracy of the suspected root cause nodes.

explanations.topologyExample: Topology example: Through deep alert analysis, you can see the complete business call relationships associated with the alert.
explanations.alertAnalysisTimeRange: Example: In deep alert analysis, dragging the time range allows viewing detailed alert information for different periods. In AI dialogue, all alerts within this time range are submitted, and each alert is already associated with the application interface.
explanations.identifySuspectedRootCause: First, let the LLM identify suspected root cause nodes based on the topology structure and alert information.
explanations.applicationAlert: 1. Application layer alerts (e.g., URL interface latency anomalies and error anomalies)
explanations.containerAlert: 2. Container alerts (e.g., K8s events such as container killed or restarted)
explanations.infrastructureAlert: 3. Infrastructure host layer alerts (e.g., CPU, memory, disk, and network throughput anomalies on hosts)
explanations.networkAlert: 4. Network layer alerts (e.g., periodic abnormal Ping values between nodes)
explanations.errorAlert: 5. Error alerts (e.g., Java programs using Java Exception, non-Java programs using log error count anomalies. This helps identify errors in microservice scenarios where errors are encapsulated in error codes, causing HTTP status codes to always be 200)
explanations.expertInsight: Expert insight: Only application layer alerts and error alerts can be transmitted along the call chain.
explanations.alertPropagationExample: As shown in the diagram, application layer alerts and error alerts propagate from downstream to upstream.
explanations.upstreamNotRootCause: The application alerts of upstream nodes are caused by transmission from downstream, so upstream nodes are not suspected root cause nodes.
explanations.alertPropagationProcess: Example of application alert propagation: ts-route-service → ts-travel-service → ts-route-plan-service → ts-gateway-service.
explanations.intermittentAlerts: If an application's interface generates intermittent alerts, they should be excluded from suspected root cause nodes.
explanations.intermittentAlertDefinition: Definition of intermittent alerts: During the troubleshooting period, the alert appears and is quickly resolved.
explanations.rootCauseAlertPropagation: Alerts from the root cause node should propagate inversely along the call chain to the business entry.
explanations.alertPropagationBreak: In the example, the alert transmission stops at a certain upstream node, indicating that neither the upstream nor downstream nodes are root cause nodes.
explanations.aiModelAccuracy: Different AI models have varying accuracy. APO uses the DeepSeek model for analysis.
explanations.configurableAiModel: Users can modify the configuration file to choose different AI models such as Zhipu, Qianfan, Doubao, etc.
